text:
olivia: Heads-up — seeing a new p95 tail on hosted text-gen over the last 20m. p50 steady, but p95 jumped ~45ms (from ~120ms -> ~165ms). Noticed correlation with small requests (<=32 tokens).
sam: Any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: new runtime canary rolled to 5% at 2026-03-23T14:02Z (rev: runtime-optim-42).
olivia: Yes canary is live, but we only started seeing the spike ~5m after. Ran a quick flamegraph from hostside sampling: tokenization ~18% of extra, request parse/headers ~12%, gRPC small-write + handshake overhead ~35% of delta. KV cache hotspots only ~8%.
jess: Can you paste the flame snippet?
olivia: ```flamegraph summary (delta p95): tokenization: 18ms, parse/headers: 12ms, grpc-writev/hpack: 16ms, tls/handshake: 10ms, kvcache-evict: 4ms, kernel-sched: 5ms```
ravi: hpack + writev jumps smell like fragmentation + tiny frames. Are we doing micro-writes on proxy->runtime path?
olivia: Yes, proxy recently switched to incremental framing to reduce memcopy (PR #891). That reduced p50 CPU but might increase syscalls for tiny payloads.
sam: For small requests, syscalls dominate. We should try coalescing window for <64B payloads. Also check tokenization: are we re-tokenizing prefix repeatedly?
jess: Good call. On a canary node I saw repeated prefix tokenization for multi-part stream clients (no prefix caching). Might be missing early KV cache warm path for streaming sessions.
perf-bot: alert: kvcache-shard-5 eviction rate +42% on canary group (15:06-15:12 UTC).
olivia: Agree — hypothesis: canary framing change increased small-write frequency -> kernel syscall overhead + HPACK encode -> slower ingress parse -> KV warm misses cascade.
ravi: Quick experiments: 1) Enable writev coalescing in proxy (batch short buffers for 2-4ms) 2) Add lightweight prefix token cache for active streams 3) Bump kvcache shard size on canary to reduce evictions.
sam: I can bench 1 & 2 locally. What's a minimal repro? olivia can you share a tiny test harness?
olivia: Repro script (run on dev box against canary):
```bash
# simulates many small text requests
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  printf 'POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nContent-Length: 4\r\n\r\nping' | nc localhost 8080 &
done
wait
```
This hits the small-fragment path. Use --stream flag for streaming clients.
jess: Also try `LD_PRELOAD=libcoalesce.so` shim to simulate writev coalesce to see perf impact before committing.
sam: Running bench now. Expect: coalesce should drop syscall count by ~60% and p95 by ~20-25ms. Token prefix cache should drop tokenization cost for stream clients by 10-15ms.
perf-bot: perf trace note: kernel-syscall rate increased x3 on canary at 15:04 UTC.
olivia: If we confirm, plan: revert canary framing change or flip on adaptive coalesce fast path for small payloads, and ship prefix-token cache as opt-in for streaming. Also add a kvcache shard auto-grow in the short term.
ravi: One more: consider moving HPACK encode to a batched worker thread to avoid blocking ingress parse path — cheap but reduces tail variance.
jess: SGTM. I'll prototype a non-blocking HPACK queue.
sam: Update: local bench with coalesce shim shows p95 delta down 28ms. Token prefix cache prototype reduces tokenization time 12ms for stream tests.
olivia: Nice. Canary rollback queued if we don't flip coalesce by 15:40. I'll add tracing hooks to measure syscall counts per request and kvcache hits.
perf-bot: reminder: open incident if p95 > 200ms for 5m across >=3 zones.
deply-bot: (typo) deploy-bot: will schedule canary flip after sam's PR lands.
jess: Assigning action items: sam -> PR for proxy coalesce shim, jess -> HPACK worker spike, olivia -> tracing + kvcache auto-grow toggle, ravi -> monitor shard evictions and suggest shard map.
olivia: Thanks — let's keep this thread for quick updates. :eyes: :+1:
